findings.title: Check the correct process type before killing unhealthy workers
findings.body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of multiprocessing.Process; those classes separately inherit BaseProcess. This check therefore skips kill() for every production worker. When a live worker hangs, its replacement overwrites the tracked handle while the original remains alive, leaking processes and allowing concurrent flushing of the same shards if the original recovers. Check against the spawn context's Process class or BaseProcess and clean up the old worker before replacing it.

findings.title: Clean up every worker after the join timeout expires
findings.body: If next_step.join() or an earlier worker consumes the timeout, this break skips cleanup for every remaining worker. Setting stopped is insufficient for workers blocked in Redis or future.result(), since they cannot inspect that flag until the operation returns. Consequently, join() can return during a rebalance while old workers remain alive and retain their shard assignments indefinitely. Apply the deadline only to graceful waiting, then terminate and reap all workers that have not exited.
